🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin slipped below $84K as the 10-year Treasury yield hit a 19-year high. Clarity Act fallout, BitMEX's exit and an $18B options expiry keep traders cautious ahead of the Trump–Xi summit. 📉 Bitcoin Slips Below $84K as 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits 19-Year High Bitcoin dropped to around $83,200 during Asian trading on Thursday after the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield closed Wednesday at 5.11%, its highest level since 2007. Strong U.S. business data, a weak five-year note auction and rebounding oil prices fueled the bond selloff, lifting bets on another Fed hike in October and wiping out roughly $510 million in leveraged crypto positions. Read full story 🏛️ White House Blames Democrats and Bank Lobby for Clarity Act Defeat White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt defended President Trump's crypto ties after the Senate failed to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, arguing Democrats turned the issue political. Witt said Trump accepted two unprecedented ethics provisions, including possible divestment or a blind trust, blamed bank lobbyists worried about stablecoin rewards, and signaled that policy work now shifts to regulators like the SEC. More details ⚖️ Kalshi Denies CFTC Probe Over $5B in Clustered Ether Perp Trades Prediction market Kalshi says the CFTC has not contacted it and that no formal examination is open, after a Wall Street Journal report said the regulator was reviewing nearly one million ether perpetual trades clustered around $5,500 each, totaling over $5 billion in a month. Kalshi attributes the pattern to its liquidity incentive program and rejects wash-trading claims. Read more 🔚 BitMEX Shuts Down After 11 Years as the Perpetuals Pioneer Exits BitMEX, the exchange co-founded by Arthur Hayes that popularized perpetual swaps, ended all trading and deposits at 04:00 UTC on September 23. Users can still log in and withdraw, but verified accounts with leftover balances face a monthly fee of $50 or 1% annualized, whichever is greater. API withdrawals remain available until September 28. See details 🤝 MoonPay to Buy SEC-Registered North Capital in $60M+ All-Stock Deal Crypto payments firm MoonPay agreed to acquire North Capital, a private-markets platform with roughly $9 billion in transaction volume, in an all-stock deal valued above $60 million.
